contracts.name: cybergraphics_api
contracts.purpose: Stable C ABI implemented by every renderer plugin.

modules.name: cyber_core
modules.purpose: Fixed-width types, assertions, logging, Result, configuration switches, versioning, hashing, and other dependency-free primitives.
invariants: No dependency on any other CyberGraphics module.
Assertions and logging must not allocate on the failure path.
Public headers are self-contained and compile on their own.
modules.tests: Unit tests for Result, assertion formatting, log channels and sinks, and version macros.
modules.budgets: Assert path: no allocation. Log path: thread-safe and bounded.

modules.name: cyber_math
modules.purpose: Scalar and SIMD math: vectors, matrices, quaternions, transforms, geometry, color, half floats.
invariants: Right-handed, +Y up, column vectors, column-major matrices, 0..1 reverse-Z.
Scalar and SIMD paths produce identical results within documented tolerance.
No heap allocation in math operations.
non_goals: SIMD dispatch beyond SSE/AVX2 in the first pass.
modules.tests: Unit tests for every operation with tolerance helpers, plus a SIMD-versus-scalar benchmark.
modules.budgets: No heap allocation. Record SIMD-versus-scalar results on the target machine.

modules.name: cyber_memory
modules.purpose: Allocator interface, linear, stack, pool, free-list and ring allocators, tracking, containers, strings, spans, and generation-counted handles.
invariants: Every runtime allocation goes through the allocator interface.
Handles carry an index and a generation.
Every container documents its copy and move rules.
modules.tests: Container stress tests, deliberate-leak report, stale-handle detection, ASan and UBSan runs.
modules.budgets: Allocator overhead documented per allocator. No hidden global allocations.

modules.name: cyber_platform
modules.purpose: Renderer-agnostic OS services: window, input, time, files, memory mapping, thread wrappers, dynamic-library loading, and a caller-owned pixel present blit.
invariants: No renderer or RHI includes.
Win32 code is isolated under src/win32/.
Unsupported platforms provide a null window backend.
Platform state is explicit; no hidden mutable globals.
File buffers and watcher state use explicit allocators.
non_goals: GPU device creation or present (cyber_rhi, cyber_software_renderer).
Audio, gamepads, clipboard, and drag-and-drop policy.
modules.tests: Window/event smoke test, timer and fixed-step tests, file I/O and memory mapping, file watcher, thread wrappers, and dynamic-library loading.
modules.budgets: Input latency and timer resolution recorded on the target machine. Window events are fixed-capacity; no per-frame heap allocation in the input path.

modules.name: cyber_perf
modules.purpose: Performance instrumentation seam: CPU and GPU markers, counters, frame statistics, budgets, and export.
invariants: Instrumentation is opt-in and near-zero cost when disabled.
No allocation on the marker hot path.
Implementations are thread-safe when used from worker threads.
non_goals: RHI timestamp query implementation (cyber_rhi consumes and produces data).
Frame capture and export in the Phase 5 seam.
modules.tests: Null profiler behavior, balanced marker scopes from the job system, and counter delivery.
modules.budgets: Disabled marker cost below 1 ns; enabled path allocation-free.

modules.name: cyber_jobs
modules.purpose: Job system: fixed worker pool, work-stealing queues, dependency counters, handles, and parallel-for.
invariants: A job never waits on work that cannot make progress.
Every submitted job has explicit dependency and completion rules.
Shutdown is deterministic and joins every worker.
Oversubscription is tested explicitly.
non_goals: Fibers and job cancellation in the first pass.
Nested ParallelFor from a worker in the first pass.
modules.tests: 10,000 jobs at 1, 2, 4, and hardware workers; dependency chains; ParallelFor coverage; oversubscription; repeated shutdown; profiler scope balance; TSan on Linux.
modules.budgets: 10,000 jobs scale across all cores; record scaling at 1, 2, 4, and N workers.

modules.name: cyber_stability
modules.purpose: Validation, diagnostics, crash handling, leak tracking, device-lost handling, and the fuzz harness.
invariants: Validation is debug-only unless explicitly enabled.
Crash paths avoid allocation.
Every reported error has a stable code and a human-readable message.
modules.tests: Deliberate leak, invalid handle, crash-handler smoke test, and validation-hook tests.
modules.budgets: Disabled validation below 1% CPU. Crash handler writes within a bounded time.

modules.name: cyber_rhi
modules.purpose: GPU hardware interface: device, queues, resources, pipelines, command lists, synchronization, swapchain, and backends.
invariants: Only this module includes D3D12, Vulkan, or Metal headers.
Synchronization is explicit; there are no hidden barriers.
Resources use generation-counted handles and deferred destruction.
The null backend validates every public operation.
non_goals: Render graph, materials, lighting, and passes (cyber_renderer).
modules.tests: Null-backend creation, lifetime and invalid-use tests; barrier validation; backend conformance suite.
modules.budgets: CPU submission cost measured. No per-draw heap allocation.

modules.name: cyber_shaders
modules.purpose: Shader language, lexer, parser, type checker, IR, HLSL/SPIR-V/MSL code generation, reflection, and permutation cache.
invariants: Compiler errors carry file, line, and column.
The compiler never crashes on malformed input; parsers are fuzz-tested.
Reflection is the single source of truth for bindings.
non_goals: Direct DXIL generation in the first pass.
modules.tests: Golden compile tests, expected-error tests, fuzz tests, and reflection layout tests.
modules.budgets: Incremental shader compile within 1 s on the target machine; cache hits avoid recompilation.

modules.name: cyber_assets
modules.purpose: Importers and decoders for glTF, OBJ, PNG, JPEG, DDS and KTX; cooked formats, asset database, and cooking.
invariants: Every parser treats input as hostile and bounds-checks before use.
Cooked files are versioned, checksummed, and memory-mappable.
No global asset state.
modules.tests: Parser unit tests, fuzz tests, cook-and-load benchmark, and golden asset round-trip.
modules.budgets: Cooked load measurably faster than source. Fuzz targets run on a schedule.

modules.name: cyber_scene
modules.purpose: Renderer-side scene: proxies, bounds, frustum culling, spatial index, and LOD selection.
invariants: Proxies are the renderer's copies; game-thread data never leaks into render-thread reads.
Culling is deterministic and matches the brute-force reference.
Bounds are tightly packed.
modules.tests: Brute-force culling comparison, plane-straddling cases, and a 100,000-object benchmark.
modules.budgets: 100,000-object cull within the budget recorded in the phase report.

modules.name: cyber_renderer
modules.purpose: Renderer architecture: render graph, passes, materials, PBR, shadows, IBL, post-processing, GI, and GPU-driven rendering.
invariants: All GPU work goes through cyber_rhi; no backend headers.
Passes declare reads and writes; barriers are graph-generated.
No game logic, only render proxies.
modules.tests: Graph culling and aliasing tests, golden images, per-pass GPU timings, and scene benchmarks.
modules.budgets: Per-pass GPU budgets live in docs/perf. Frame-time percentiles are tracked.

modules.name: cyber_ui
modules.purpose: Immediate-mode UI, debug overlay, text, graphs, console variables, and the render graph viewer.
invariants: UI draws only through the graphics API and works on GPU and software renderers.
No per-frame allocation in steady state.
Input routing is deterministic.
modules.tests: Golden UI image on both renderers, input routing tests, and a no-allocation steady-state test.
modules.budgets: UI CPU cost below the budget recorded in the phase report.

modules.name: cyber_capture
modules.purpose: Frame capture: record RHI commands and resources, versioned capture format, and replay hooks.
invariants: Capture format is versioned and backend-neutral.
Replay is deterministic within tolerance.
Capture overhead is bounded and opt-in.
modules.tests: Record and replay round-trip, cross-backend replay, and format version compatibility.
modules.budgets: Capture overhead recorded. No overhead when disabled.

modules.name: cyber_graphics
modules.purpose: The CyberGraphics GPU renderer product: plugin entry, backend selection, frame loop, and implementation of the stable API.
invariants: Implements only the stable API in include/cybergraphics/.
No public C++ types cross the plugin boundary.
Capability negotiation is explicit.
modules.tests: Plugin ABI compatibility, backend switch, and golden images against the software reference.
modules.budgets: Frame budgets live in docs/perf. CPU submission cost measured.

modules.name: cyber_software_renderer
modules.purpose: CPU reference renderer: framebuffer, rasterization, depth, textures, shaders, golden images, and the second plugin.
invariants: No RHI dependency; pure CPU.
Deterministic output for golden images.
Color is stored linear; the renderer converts to sRGB only when pixels leave it.
Implements the stable API in include/cybergraphics/ when Phase 25 lands.
modules.tests: Golden images at 640x360, raster coverage, clipping, and API conformance.
modules.budgets: Golden-image suite runtime budget. Small test resolution.
